failures.criterion: Acceptance 6 of dispatch://INFRA-750/spec: the suites pass at the head, and the pull request is one a reviewer can approve and the daemon can merge. The base's required checks must have run at the head, since the reviewer reads the head's checks before it approves and a base that requires a check will not merge a head whose checks never ran.

The newest run of this pull request is 41003417826 (CI, conclusion success) at d810c7aebaba5e5b02a7e89f080389f562b7466a, the second of the ten commits of this generation; `gh run list --repo sjawhar/legion --branch legion/INFRA-750 --limit 50` lists no run at any later commit. Cause: the push that carried the seven code commits ab30ae89ba7a, f0f9fc6f64c0, a91f3cd84d37, 3ec6980b6afc, 25395fff0760, 3a8b767296bb and 725e26a83afa ended at f228f29d, whose message is `implement: record handoff` with `skip-checks: true` as its last line after two empty lines (`jj log -r f228f29d --no-graph -T description | cat -A` shows the shape), so GitHub started no workflow run for that push. Only a push whose commits touch only `.legion/<issue>/` carries that trailer (skill://legion-worker/references/skip-checks-trailer.md); this push also carried internal/bus/stream.go, keeper.go, settings.go, nats.go, bustest, cmd/listener, cmd/dispatch, the docs, packages/envoy-client, packages/claude-envoy and the simplify pass, none of which any CI lane has ever read. No red test pins this: it is a property of the branch at GitHub, not of the code. Remedy, for the implementer: rewrite f228f29d's message without the trailer (`jj describe -r <commit> --config 'templates.commit_trailers=""' -m "implement: record handoff"`), then `jj bookmark set legion/INFRA-750 -r @- --allow-backwards` and push once, which starts the run; a body edit starts none while the head carries the trailer.

proof.criterion: The listener notices a dead hub in seconds (the spec's `Also in the second pull request` acceptance): a test stops answering the listener's pings without closing its socket, and the listener reports the connection lost within 5 seconds.
proof.surface: The real envoy-listener binary, started as production starts it with the live topics lane on, against an in-process NATS whose relay stops moving bytes in both directions with both sides' connections kept (testnats.Server.Freeze).
proof.observed: 3 of 3 passed (5.91 s, 5.20 s, 5.28 s). The `envoy` client reported the cut 2.789 s, 2.787 s and 2.791 s after the freeze; the `envoy-live-topics` client 2.839 s, 2.838 s and 2.841 s. Both are inside the 5 s the acceptance asks for.
proof.negativeControl: Each call site was broken on its own, with the test file untouched. `bus.WithSilentCutDetection()` removed from openLiveTopics alone: `--- FAIL ... no disconnect line for envoy-live-topics 5.019s into a silent cut`, with `envoy`'s `nats: stale connection` line present. The same option removed from listenerStreamOptions alone: `--- FAIL ... no disconnect line for envoy 5.025s into a silent cut`, with `envoy-live-topics`'s line present. Both files were restored with `jj restore` and `jj status` is clean of them.

proof.criterion: The daemon notices a dead hub in seconds (the INFRA-14 architect's decision of 2026-10-30): the same ping settings at the daemon's one NATS connection, with a frozen-server test inside the same bound.
proof.surface: The daemon's own natsauth.Connect, called as internal/daemon/workflow.go:366 calls it (LogEvents and ReconnectForever), against a server that answers the handshake PING and then answers nothing with the socket open.
proof.observed: 2 of 2 passed under -race (ok 7.077s). The cut was noticed 3.020823347 s and 3.006805133 s after the server went quiet, with `NATS connection lost` in the captured log and IsConnected false.
proof.negativeControl: `options = append(options, detectSilentCuts)` removed from Connect, the test file untouched: `--- FAIL ... the connection was not reported lost within 5.010739211s of the server going quiet: IsConnected = true, the warning logged = false`. natsauth.go was restored with `jj restore`.

proof.criterion: Item 1.8: startDispatchStream waits for this client's own reconcile, so a check that the next start wrote nothing cannot pass before that start wrote anything.
proof.surface: The Dispatch server's start on one in-process NATS server, through the helper production's own test uses, with JetStream's API watched for every write.
proof.command: From packages/envoy: `go test -count=1 -timeout 30m ./cmd/dispatch/`, which runs TestADefaultDispatchStartOnASingleServerCreatesEverythingAtOneCopyAndTheNextWritesNothing and TestADispatchStartKeepsAThreeCopyStreamsCopiesByteLimitAndIDAsItCorrectsTheStream over bustest.StreamDrifts.
proof.observed: ok github.com/sjawhar/envoy/cmd/dispatch 51.317s. The helper's wait is sound on this path: cmd/dispatch's client is always a background one (dispatchClientOptions at cmd/dispatch/main.go:1201 passes bus.WithConnectInBackground), and a background owning client registers ensureStreamOnce inside its constructor, so its first connection raises the hooked count the helper waits on.
proof.negativeControl: The write-nothing property was broken rather than the test: `if reflect.DeepEqual(desired, info.Config)` in ensureStreamWithConfig (internal/bus/stream.go:426) disabled, so every start writes. `--- FAIL ... the second start wrote [$JS.API.STREAM.UPDATE.ENVOY_NOTIFICATIONS], want nothing`. stream.go was restored with `jj restore`.

proof.criterion: A hub that comes back after a silent cut leaves the listener working: the new pings must not trade a half-open connection for a client that redials and loses its watchers. The pull request's own risk section says a false cut `costs a redial`; this drives that redial.
proof.surface: The real envoy-listener binary with the live lane on, frozen until both clients reported the cut, then thawed, with an interest written through a second connection afterwards and read back through the listener's own GET /v1/interests/.
proof.command: A throwaway test in packages/envoy/cmd/listener (TestTheListenerComesBackAfterASilentCut), run with `go test -count=1 -timeout 10m -v -run 'TestTheListenerComesBackAfterASilentCut$' ./cmd/listener/` and removed afterwards, since it pins no defect.
proof.observed: PASS in 8.69 s: both clients reported the cut 2.837 s after it began, both logged `envoy nats reconnected` 1.109 s after the thaw, the interest another listener wrote after the thaw reached this listener's cache 4 ms later, and /healthz answered healthy again. Two ERROR lines are logged during the redial, `interest registry watch failed` and `role claims watch failed`, each `nats: connection closed`, from the first watcher's goroutine after the rewatch has already replaced it (internal/kvwatch/kvwatch.go:202); a server restart logs none, which TestListenerFollowsTheInterestRegistryAcrossNATSRestarts asserts. Recorded as an observation, not a failure: the lines are not new behaviour, the cut path reached them before this change too, and no alert of this deployment reads a log level (packages/envoy/infra/README.md and infra/docs/nats-hub.md name metric alerts only). What is new is how often that path is reached: any hub silence over about two seconds now takes it.
proof.negativeControl: The freeze is the control, and the reading is scoped to it: every line the run judges is taken from the listener's output after the freeze began (the run records the output's length first and reads only what follows), and the run leaves its first phase only once both clients have reported the connection lost, 2.837 s in. So the `envoy nats reconnected` lines and the interest read back are the thaw's doing and cannot be a healthy connection from before the cut. The same freeze without the production change is the listener never reporting the cut at all, which the two call-site controls of the first proof entry show.
